Placing a placeholder description here for now.

Became an enterprise-ready developer in six months as part of the CODA 13 cohort. Graduated into TDP after completing my Dojo project in Cyber Intel building a MERN stack feature for a security remediation platform. Spent my first rotation in Cyber IAM wearing many hats (frontend, design, infrastructure, etc.) maintaining custom authorization plugins, and ended up finishing the program in Cyber D&M as a full stack engineer for our self-service platform.

Started my research career in the applied sociology field with Amy Donley building maps for drug policy white papers in the ISBS. Joined the STIR Lab under Pamela Wisniewski shortly after to help with the IGDD project, which then turned into MOSafely. Finally, worked with Jonathan Powell to maintain CoupCast and wrote some articles with Salah Ben Hammou, his PhD student.
As part of Making Augmented and Virtual Reality Accessible, I built assistive technology prototypes for blind and low vision users in the CEAL Lab under Brian Smith.

In Spatial Models and Electoral Distrciting, I applied TDA algorithms on ACS datasets from Mecklenburg County to identify communities of interest and collaborated with Jim Thatcher and Courtney Thatcher from the University of Puget Sound.
Called low-propensity voters, handwrote outreach letters, and tried my best to get Democratic candidates down the ballot elected across Florida, Georgia, and Texas.

Including: PMBF Program, UNA-Orlando, BallotReady, The COVID-19 Tracking Project, Council on Foreign Relations, the Hub Project, Swing Left, New America, ActBlue, KRC Research, and ActBlue Technical Services.
